settings.g: Crew rest and the working day

items.name: Crew rest
items.line: The rest a flyer needs before his day starts. The crew-rest warning and the tight crew-rest advisory move with it.

items.name: Days in a row
items.line: A day on the programme beyond this many in a row raises the red break-day warning.

items.name: Long work day
items.line: A longer day, first commitment to last, shows the grey long-day note.

items.name: Default rally before take-off
items.line: An empty R box, a formation's rally, suggests a time this long before take-off, and "+ In-time" fills in that same time. When no in-time or rally is entered, a flyer's day starts at that time: his long day, OIL and Insights hours count from it. The tight crew-rest advisory also checks his rest as if he reported at that time.

items.name: Brief before take-off
items.line: Sets the suggested B on a line with no brief typed, and a blank B is checked against it. With no in-time typed, crew rest counts to this B. A published day keeps its B until it is published again.

items.name: Step before take-off
items.line: A man counts as busy from step: conflicts and the crew list follow it. It and dekit set the shortest tight turn. It also decides when a LATE SHOW crew-rest ring turns from dashed to solid.

items.name: Dekit after landing
items.line: A man counts as busy until dekit. It and step set the shortest tight turn.

items.name: Debrief after landing
items.line: Ends a flyer's day: tomorrow's crew rest, the long day, OIL and Insights hours count to here, and so does the flight debrief advisory.

items.name: Tight turn
items.line: A shorter gap from landing to the next take-off is a tight turn. It is never less than dekit plus step.

items.name: In-time words
items.line: What "+ In-time" writes after the time.

items.name: EP sim brief
items.line: The brief before an EP sim, unless its remarks name one.

items.name: Sim debrief
items.line: The debrief after a sim.

items.name: AMT debrief
items.line: How long an AMT debrief runs when its DEBRIEF row has no end.

items.name: A flight
items.line: A flight with a take-off and no landing is taken to land this long after take-off. Conflicts, the tight turn, the debrief, crew rest, the long day, OIL and Insights hours count to that landing, and its warnings say it was assumed.

items.name: A sim
items.line: A sim with a start and no end is taken to run this long, for conflicts and the crew list. It earns no OIL until its end is typed.

items.name: Any other row
items.line: The same for a ground, programme or duty row.

items.name: SC day window
items.line: A shift wholly inside it needs SC DAY; one reaching outside it needs SC NIGHT.

items.name: SC MAIN conflicts
items.line: What an SC MAIN man's conflict with each shows: a red warning or an amber advisory. Once his shift flies, every conflict is red.

items.name: Inputs late cut-off
items.line: An input last changed after it wears LATE.

items.name: SANS late cut-off
items.line: The same for SANS availability.

items.name: Members file for others
items.line: A member may file a duty or commitment for someone else. Never leave, medical or SANS availability.

items.name: Full day of OIL
items.line: Weekend or holiday work this long or longer earns a full day; less earns a half.

items.name: Track Blue and Red sorties
items.line: Splits Insights' flying bars into Blue and Red, and asks Blue or Red under a formation.

checks.g: Crew rest and the working day

items.name: Crew rest (<12h)
items.line: For a flying member: at least 12h (Crew rest) from the end of his day before to his earliest in-time, or to anything earlier that day.
how: Rest runs from the end of the day before to the first thing today: his in-time or rally, his B where neither is typed, or anything earlier, such as a meeting.

The day before ends at its last commitment of any kind. A flight ends at landing plus the debrief (2h), or, where no landing is typed, at the assumed landing (A flight, 1h after take-off) plus the debrief. Anything else ends at its written end. A standby shift, or a desk made from an SC, AVALON or BB template, with START typed and END blank is left out until its END is typed.
An input counts only if it is a duty or commitment, other than Personal or SANS Availability, with typed times.
Exactly 12h is legal. A day with no flying asks for no rest.
A LATE SHOW remark keeps the warning. The ring is dashed while rest still clears by step, solid after.
Monday checks last Sunday. A Sunday that breaks Monday shows a "Breaks Monday" box.
A flying line with no times yet is not measured, but a typed brief, in-time or landing on it still counts.
An SC SPARE standing by carries no crew rest either way, but one that flies carries it as any flyer does. A shift reports at its start, or at its B or R where one is earlier than the start.

items.name: Tight turning
items.line: His rest would be short if he reported the usual 3h before take-off (Default rally before take-off), but his in-time or rally, or his B where neither is typed, is later, so his rest clears.

items.name: Days in a row
items.line: On the programme more than 6 days in a row.
how: Any tasking counts: a flight, a duty, a sim, a ground or programme row.
Leave or a downchit resets the count.
It counts last week's tail, and the warning lands on the day to clear.

items.name: Long day
items.line: More than 12h from first commitment to last.

items.name: Conflict
items.line: Two commitments overlap for one man. Touching end to end is not a conflict.

items.name: Overlaps standby
items.line: An SC MAIN man is also down for something set to Advisory under SC MAIN conflicts. A commitment input across the shift is red; a meeting stays amber. Once the shift flies, every conflict with it is red.

items.name: ⓘ info only
items.line: A ground or programme item marked ⓘ is printed but never checked, and earns no OIL.

items.name: Past midnight
items.line: A row whose end reads earlier than its start runs into the next day.

items.name: Flying wave
items.line: An ordinary flying wave — it counts toward the day’s flying tally, and every line is fully cross-checked.

items.name: In-time / Rally — timings out of order
items.line: In-time, rally, brief, take-off and landing are not in that order.
how: The order is in-time, rally, brief, take-off, landing. Equal times are fine.
The B on the line is what is checked. A blank B is checked as the suggested brief, take-off less 2h20.
Out of order is red, but it never stops a day being published.
A formation's rally is its R box alone. An In-time line is an in-time whatever its words, even one that says RALLY, and its first clock is used (09:00H or 0900).
A formation's name makes the line that formation's; otherwise it is the whole wave's.
A clock later than take-off means the day before.
A line with no clock, RALLY AFTER IN TIME included, sets no time.

items.name: In-time — check the reporting instruction
items.line: The app cannot read the clock on an In-time line.

items.name: Misses flight brief
items.line: Something sits between the brief and take-off. A blank B counts as the suggested one (Brief before take-off).

items.name: Misses flight debrief
items.line: Something sits inside landing plus 2h (Debrief after landing).

items.name: Tight turn
items.line: Less than 2h from landing to the next take-off (Tight turn, or Dekit plus Step if longer).

items.name: Double turning
items.line: Two or more sorties in one day. One line names everyone; it is routine, not an error.

items.name: Flight times — take-off and landing are the same
items.line: A line's take-off and landing are the same time. A flying line still earns its OIL from the report before it and the debrief after it, and none if it has neither. A standby shift with no length earns none. One that flies with its R or B before its START earns from that time.

items.name: Misses sim brief
items.line: Something sits inside an EP sim's 15 min brief (EP sim brief), or an AMT's BRIEF row.

items.name: Misses sim debrief
items.line: Something sits inside a sim's 30 min debrief (Sim debrief), or an AMT's DEBRIEF row (AMT debrief, where that row has no end).

items.name: Illegal seat
items.line: A man in a seat he may not hold, such as a WSO in the front seat. Any pilot may fly the rear seat.

items.name: Crew not authorised
items.line: An OCU pilot with a CAT A–D WSO, or the reverse. An instructor in either seat clears it.

items.name: Crew solo — only allowed under syllabus
items.line: An OCU pilot with an OCU WSO. Allowed only on sorties the syllabus names.

items.name: CO approval needed
items.line: A CAT D pilot with a CAT C WSO, a CAT C pilot with a CAT D WSO, or two CAT Ds. The crew needs the CO's approval.

items.name: OCU with no IP
items.line: An OCU formation with no instructor (IW, IP, IR or FI).

items.name: Incentive passenger — crew pairing needs approval
items.line: Ground crew in a rear seat. The ride needs approval. Ground crew are checked for conflicts, the long day, days in a row and their own absences, and a front seat is always a warning. None of the flying rules apply to them: crew rest, turns, pairing, AAR, SC currency or briefs.

items.name: IRT with no IR examiner
items.line: IRT in the mission needs an IR in the formation; IRT in an aircraft's remarks needs one in that aircraft.

items.name: AAR currency — not qualified
items.line: AAR in the remarks needs the front seat's currency: night on a night wave, day otherwise. NAAR or DAAR says it outright.

items.name: AAR — back seat not cleared to instruct
items.line: A pilot not current may fly AAR as training only with an instructor pilot (IP, IR or FI) in the back seat marked I for it on Quals (an I in place of the tick on DAAR or NAAR). That clears the front seat's currency warning, but an instructor pilot without the mark is flagged instead.

items.name: SC currency — wrong shift
items.line: A standby shift wholly inside 07:00 to 19:00 (SC day window) needs SC DAY; one reaching outside it needs SC NIGHT. A SPARE is checked the same as a MAIN.

items.name: Night after day
items.line: NAAR needs DAAR, and SC NIGHT needs SC DAY. On Quals, removing the day one removes the night one.

items.name: SC
items.line: A SPARE line is only checked for overseas / medically down, SC currency, a pilots-only front seat and not holding another SC seat or SC desk in the same hours — nothing else, unless it flies. A MAIN line is checked in full. Add as many of each as you need.

items.name: AVALON
items.line: Overnight. Every line — MAIN or SPARE — is only checked for overseas / medically down, SC NIGHT currency, a pilots-only front seat and not holding another AVALON seat or the AVALON desk in the same hours. Nothing else, unless it flies. Add as many as you need.

items.name: BB
items.line: Times are yours to set. The same checks as AVALON — overseas / medically down, SC currency for the hours typed, a pilots-only front seat and not holding another seat or the BB desk in the same hours. Nothing else, unless it flies. Add as many as you need.

items.name: A shift's hours
items.line: A standby shift takes exactly its written hours: no step, dekit, brief or debrief.

items.name: A standby row that flies
items.line: A shift with its B or R typed flies, every row on it; a row ticked FLIES on the Scheduler Board flies on its own. A row that flies has its conflicts and turns checked as a sortie's are, counts as a jet and a sortie, and earns OIL by default. A row with nobody on it counts nothing; one that does not come in is cancelled with CX.

items.name: Standby line flies — no start or end
items.line: A standby shift that flies has no START or END, so its crew rest and OIL cannot be worked out.

items.name: Busy before a standby shift
items.line: A standby row that flies has a typed B (the crew's in-time) or R (its rally), whichever is earlier, and something sits between it and the shift start. That time also starts his crew rest, his long day and his OIL.

items.name: Arming an SC seat
items.line: The crew list judges each man against that shift's hours only.

items.name: An input closes its hours
items.line: Every input closes the man for the hours it covers, from the moment it is filed. One a scheduler has taken off the programme closes nothing.

items.name: On leave + planned
items.line: A man on leave is planned for a flight, sim, duty or ground slot.

items.name: Downchit + planned
items.line: A medically down man is planned. On ATT B he may still stand a duty, sim or ground slot, but not fly.

items.name: Conflict with a request
items.line: Any other input conflicts with a planned slot: a course, a meeting, an appointment, overseas duty.

items.name: A seat with no times
items.line: Still checked against an absence covering the whole day; a part-day absence waits until the seat has times.

items.name: Half days
items.line: Leave and medical can be AM (to 12:00), PM (from 12:01) or all day, and a half day closes only its own half. A sortie counts from its step (Step before take-off), so AM leave still conflicts with a wave that steps before noon.

items.name: Standing SC SPARE
items.line: A man on local leave may still stand SC SPARE. Overseas leave or duty (OL, OD) or a medical code (HL, OML, ATT C, ATT B) may not: that is a warning. A row that flies has no such allowance.

items.name: SANS availability — planned outside the availability filed
items.line: A SANS man planned outside the event or the hours he filed. Filing nothing raises nothing.

items.name: LATE
items.line: An input last changed after its cut-off (Inputs late cut-off) wears LATE: a mark, never a warning. Downchits never do.

items.name: Weekend and holiday work earns OIL
items.line: Work on a weekend or public holiday earns OIL once the day is published: a full day or a half, by Full day of OIL.
how: Weekend or holiday work earns OIL once the day is published.
A man's day runs from his first report to his last end, gaps included: 6h01 or more is a full day (FO), less is a half (HO).

A flight runs from its in-time or rally, whichever is earlier (Default rally before take-off where neither is entered), to landing plus the debrief. With no landing typed, it lands at its assumed landing (A flight).
Any other row the scheduler adds with no times, or no end time, earns nothing, but a request answered yes earns over its own times. An Off day earns nothing.
SC SPARE, AVALON and BB rows that do not fly earn only if switched on in OIL Earn. A row that flies earns by default, from its B or R if earlier than its START, otherwise from its START, to its END.
Until its wave flies, a desk made from an AVALON or BB template earns only if switched on in OIL Earn. Once the wave flies, the desk earns by default.
A Duty & commitments input earns once its OIL question is answered yes.
A published day keeps its OIL until it is published again.

items.name: No OIL earned — a row has no usable times
items.line: On a weekend or holiday, a row with someone on it and no usable times earns nobody on it any OIL. The warning names the row.

items.name: OIL waiting — this day is not published
items.line: A weekend or holiday with someone to earn is not published yet. Nobody earns until it is.

items.name: No OIL — no Leave War period covers this date
items.line: No Leave War period covers this weekend or holiday, so its work earns nobody OIL. The day offers to create the period, before and after it is published.

items.name: Became a holiday after publishing — republish for its OIL
items.line: A day published as a working day that the Leave War now calls a public holiday earns nothing until it is published again.

items.name: No longer a holiday — republish to withdraw its OIL
items.line: A day published as a holiday that the Leave War no longer calls one keeps its OIL until it is published again, which withdraws it.

items.name: Published before these seats counted — republish to credit them
items.line: A weekend or holiday published before the app counted an ALL AVAIL on a duty desk, sim or extra people line shows a pending change. Publish it again and the men behind that puck get their OIL.

items.name: Several problems on one puck
items.line: It shows the most serious flag, in this order, and its ring the most serious colour. A red box round the whole puck marks a conflict, a crew-rest breach, a qualification problem or a missed brief.

chips.label: Crew pairing — not an authorised pairing
Crew pairing — this pairing needs approval
Advisory — on shift and also down for a ground event or programme item, or planned outside SANS availability
